messages:
maria: Heads-up from the atlas-embed bringup: int4-perchannel prototype looks promising on LUT recall but flops on short queries and noisy separators.
dan: how big a flop? numbers? :chart_with_downwards_trend: 
maria: baseline fp16 recall@1 on anchor-5k = 0.741, int4_perchannel calibrated = 0.735 overall. but for queries <8 tokens with punctuation/noise recall@1 drops to 0.48 (int4) vs 0.69 (fp16). recall@5 less severe.
sophia: interesting — did you apply whitening/centering after quant? or calibrate on clean-only data?
maria: initial calibration used clean anchor set only. I ran a quick whitening + mean-centering step post-quant and saw short-query recall rise ~+0.05. command used: ```bash
./run_eval.sh --model atlas-embed-pro --quant int4_perchannel --calib s3://redwood-evals/atlas/calib/clean-10k.json --postproc whiten,normalize --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette,purity
```
dan: nice. any change in silhouette / cluster purity?
maria: silhouette fp16=0.39, int4 raw=0.33, int4+whiten=0.36. purity@k5: fp16=0.78, int4_raw=0.66, int4_whiten=0.73.
infra-bot: node-health: node-gamma reported 2 soft fallbacks to fp16 kernel during int4 run (no OOM). Kernel mismatch id: k-qt-17.
dan: @infra-bot can you dump kernel logs? could be quant kernel using different rounding path.
infra-bot: logs uploaded to s3://infra-logs/atlas/kernels/k-qt-17.log.
sophia: hypothesis: tokenization produces many single-char tokens for short queries with punctuation; quantization reduces angular resolution near origin so tiny tokens blow up cosine difference. can we compare angular histogram per-token-length?
maria: queued that. also tried small multiplicative rescale before L2 norm (scale factors 0.9, 1.0, 1.1). 1.05 improved short-query recall by ~0.03 for int4_whiten.
dan: curious if per-channel symmetric clipping vs asymmetric helps. smaller clipping range might help preserve sign.
sophia: also test a calibration set augmented with punctuation/noise; if calibration distribution mismatch, quantizer will pick wrong dynamic ranges.
eval-bot: rundata:
- model: atlas-embed-pro
- experiments: fp16, int4_perchannel_raw, int4_perchannel_whiten, int4_perchannel_whiten_noisycalib, int8_hybrid
- evalset: anchor-5k + short-query-noise-aug (punc/whitespace/char-drop)
- note: int4_whiten_noisycalib improved short-query recall@1 from 0.48 -> 0.59 but still below fp16 0.69

maria: sample of noisy-short queries uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/atlas/noisy-short-samples.txt. includes things like: 
- "what's new?" --> tokenized into [what, ', s, new, ?]
- "install - pkgmgr" --> tokenized as [install, -, pkgmgr]

dan: next runs: A) int4 symmetric clip with noisy calibration; B) per-channel quant with 2-bit mantissa hybrid (first 32 dims fp16); C) histogram of cosine distribution for matched pairs across quant modes.
sophia: add recall@1 broken down by topological cluster size (small clusters <10, medium, large) — quantization might collapse small clusters.
maria: queued runs and will post results. if int4 can't reach an operational threshold on short/noisy queries we should gate the canary and ship int8 hybrid first.
dan: agreed. also tag runtime team to look at kernel mismatch. @infra-bot any ETA on k-qt-17 fix?
infra-bot: kernel team paged. ETA 4h.
eval-bot: new run queued: 4461122356 (int4_perchannel_whiten_noisycalib)
maria: thx all — will update thread with the run summary and a concise rollback criterion (short-query recall@1 within 0.08 of fp16) once runs complete. :thumbsup:
sophia: thanks — good diagnostics. try also a tiny additive bias correction (per-dim) after quant to shift centroid back to fp16 mean. could be fast to test.
dan: yup add that to the sweep.
